findings: GPT scored 97.88/100 over 12 held-out tasks repeated twice: 19/24 attempts passed every criterion. The two repetitions scored 98.23 and 97.54; this is within-set variation, not an industry confidence interval.

On six development tasks, the GPT evidence checklist and final verification reminders both produced zero measured improvement. In the next matched six-task panel, DeepSeek verification raised score by 2.97 points and all-pass from 2/6 to 3/6; Qwen verification raised score by 0.83 but reduced all-pass from 1/6 to 0/6. No universal prompt improvement was established.

Exact-format grading can reject semantically correct answers: GPT's "Medical attachment M-2" was rejected where the rubric required "M-2". Scores are preserved under frozen v0.2; identifier normalization and semantic memo grading need independent calibration.
All five complete holdout panels recorded zero marked critical failures. This small fictional sample cannot establish safety in real insurance work.

The cases, prompts, tools and scoring were frozen for holdout. A budget-lock contention repair changed the accounting source fingerprint only; GPT uses the original fingerprint and the final Bedrock panels use the amended one. These share the visible protocol and corpus, but are not identical source snapshots.
